title: Discounted Online Convex Optimization: Uniform Regret Across a Continuous Interval
claim: Prior meta-expert frameworks combine experts under plain regret; ours must combine experts that each use a different discount factor under discounted regret.
layout: 2 stacked panels split by a horizontal rule, trees top-down, math beside nodes
description: Two stacked panels are separated by a thin horizontal line. Each panel shows a tree. A red circle labeled 'Meta-algorithm' sits at the top, and blue circles for experts sit below it, joined by black lines. The upper panel is the previous work. It has N experts, each with its own step size η_i, and dashed boxes around the meta-algorithm and the expert row. Block arrows point to the standard regret sums: the meta-algorithm's regret against the best expert, and each expert's regret against a fixed comparator. A red note says 'Track the best η* to obtain optimal Regret(T)'. The lower panel is the discounted setting. It has the same tree shape, with experts using λ_1 through λ_N. The discount weights λ^{T-t} are highlighted in red inside the regret formulas. The eye goes first to the red meta-algorithm nodes and the red discount terms.
caption: A meta-expert framework for OCO that adapts to unknown parameters (previous work, upper panel) and discounted OCO (our setting, lower panel).
abstract: Reflecting the greater significance of recent history over the distant past in non-stationary environments, $Î»$-discounted regret has been introduced in online convex optimization (OCO) to gracefully forget past data as new information arrives. When the discount factor $Î»$ is given, online gradient descent with an appropriate step size achieves an $O(1/\sqrt{1-Î»})$ discounted regret. However, the value of $Î»$ is often not predetermined in real-world scenarios. This gives rise to a significant open question: is it possible to develop a discounted algorithm that adapts to an unknown discount factor. In this paper, we affirmatively answer this question by providing a novel analysis to demonstrate that smoothed OGD (SOGD) achieves a uniform $O(\sqrt{\log T/1-Î»})$ discounted regret, holding for all values of $Î»$ across a continuous interval simultaneously. The basic idea is to maintain multiple OGD instances to handle different discount factors, and aggregate their outputs sequentially by an online prediction algorithm named as Discounted-Normal-Predictor (DNP) (Kapralov and Panigrahy,2010). Our analysis reveals that DNP can combine the decisions of two experts, even when they operate on discounted regret with different discount factors.
